name: Alternating Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: The alternating straight-arm pulldown performs the movement one arm at a time in alternating fashion from a high cable pulley, keeping constant tension on the lats throughout the set. The alternating rhythm ensures that one side is always under load, increasing total time under tension and providing a brief stretch to each lat while the opposite side contracts.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a high cable with two single handle attachments (or a wide bar you can use one hand at a time). Grasp one handle in each hand. Arms extended overhead.
execution.setup_instructions: If a single rope is used, perform one complete set on one side then switch. For true alternating, two single handles on separate cables are ideal.
steps: Step 1: Begin with both arms extended overhead.
Step 2: Pull the right arm down in a straight-arm arc to the hip while left remains overhead.
Step 3: Return the right arm as the left pulls down.
Step 4: Alternate continuously for the desired rep count.
Step 5: One rep = one pull each side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously with the alternating rhythm.
common_mistakes: Losing the stretch on the extended arm — let it reach fully overhead
safety_considerations: Light loads — this is a mind-muscle connection and stretch-focused exercise
Keep the shoulders away from the ears throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead extension to hip level on each arm.
coaching_cues: Keep the working arm straight throughout
Let the resting arm reach overhead fully
Feel the lat on each side independently
